items.title: Delhi SIR: Plea in Supreme Court challenges ECI directive requiring deleted voters to enrol afresh
items.summary: An application has been filed before the Supreme Court challenging the Election Commission of India's (ECI) requirement that voters excluded from Delhi's draft electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) must declare themselves as first-time applicants to secure restoration of their names. The application has been moved by RTI activist Anjali Bhardwaj and another petitioner in their pending petition against the Election Commission. They have sought directions to provide a separate mechanism for restoring the names of previously enrolled voters. The petitioners have pointed out that 47,56,722 electors, constituting 32.78% of Delhi's electorate before the SIR, were excluded from the draft electoral rolls published on August 31. Of these, 31,59,213 were classified as permanently shifted. According to the application, these voters must submit Form 6 to seek re-inclusion, although the form requires applicants to declare that they are seeking enrolment for the first time. items.title: ​No, Neha didn’t use a guerrilla tactic, romanticising the term hurts dissent
items.summary: Did the All India Students’ Association (AISA) leader Neha Bora use a doppelganger to evade Delhi police during the October 11 protests? Neha clarified that she hadn’t set out to do that at all. “It was not a strategy but a simple coincidence," she said later the same day on Instagram. But social media and news platforms had already rushed to characterise a case of mistaken identities as a “strategy” or "battlefield tactic”. Neha was immediately showered in praise for cleverly “ outsmarting ” authorities. To call a coincidence a manoeuvre of war is a dangerous misrepresentation of facts. It leaves peaceful civilian protesters, most of them in their 20s and 30s, vulnerable to a narrative that frames nonviolent dissent as active combat. What happened? On October 11, the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) and various Left student bodies, including AISA, called for protests amid the demand for Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. Neha asked protestors to gather at RK Ashram Marg in New Delhi at 2.30 pm. “See you there. Don’t be late,” she signed off. The number of protesters and journalists swelled at RK Ashram.
